In the WHO European Region, which covers 53 Member States across Europe and central Asia, floods are the most common natural hazard leading to emergencies.
Floods cause extensive damage, disruption and adverse health effects, particularly given the potential for increased transmission of water- and vector-borne diseases.

The impacts of floods on health arise directly through contact with floodwater as well as indirectly from damage to health facilities, other critical infrastructure, ecosystems, food and water supplies, and social support systems.
Such impacts can be immediate, but can also occur days, weeks or even months after floodwater has receded.
